description.narrative: Insatsen syftar till att stärka lokala demokratiska strukturer och bidra till skapandet av ett mer inkluderande, sammanhängande och ansvarstagande samhälle som kommer att resultera i en förbättring av levnadsvillkoren för medborgare i Zimbabwe.

The intervention seeks to strengthen democratic culture and contribute to the creation of a more inclusive, cohesive and accountable society which will result in the improvement of living conditions for citizens in Zimbabwe.

The intervention is expected to acheive the following: 1.1 Development objectiveEnhanced democratic governance contributing to improved living conditions for citizens in Zimbabwe 1.2 Overall Programme Objective (Impact)Citizens are enjoying their rights to quality and gender responsive social services from transparent and accountable local authorities 1.3 Expected outcomesOutcome 1: Increased meaningful participation of citizens (women, men, young people and vulnerable people) in selected rural and urban areas in local governance Outcome 2: Enhanced transparency and accountability of local government systems and structures in selected rural and urban local authorities. Outcome 3: Strengthened capacity of selected civil society organisations to effectively support citizens (women, men, young people and vulnerable people) to meaningfully participate in local governance and influence policies and budgets.

Key achievements from Diakonia's final report:
- In total, the programme reached 130 000 rights holders that actively participated in different local governance platforms. Of these participants, more than 70 000 (54%) were women and more than 26 000 (20%) youth.
- Consortium partners successfully lobbied the President for the 30% quota for women representation at local government level, which was endorsed by Cabinet. As a follow-up, the programme successfully advocated for the 30% quota to be part of Constitutional Amendment No 2.
- Consortium partners furthermore lobbied for a youth quota. In response, recommendations for legal modalities were made to amend the Constitution to increase the youth quota from 10 to 25% as contained in Constitutional Amendment No 2. In addition, Gwanda Rural District Council adopted a Youth Policy, which was followed by practical involvement of youth into the structures of the Local Authority (LA) from village to district development committees.
- 593 women and 762 youth (325 female, 437 male) were elected in local leadership structures - such as Junior Councils, Chief's advisors, and Waterpoint/School/Village/Ward Development Committees - across various project areas during the project period.
- The citizen's monitoring role, under the auspices of the programme, led to local authorities addressing service delivery priorities of communities, thereby increasing transparency on budgets and public resources and a subsequent reduction in corrupt activities and excessive expenditures. For instance, in 2019, Bulawayo City Councils proposed supplementary budget was reduced after the residents plea that it was too high. During the same year, advocacy for transparent use of the 3% retention fees saw the re-opening of recreation facilities such as swimming pools in Mpopoma ward 9 and Luveve Ward 15.
- In the same year, Consortium partner BPRA led a campaign to have councilors declare their assets and financial interest as a strategy of arresting runaway corruption in the Bulawayo City Council (BCC). BPRA further developed a policy framework to operationalize asset declaration. This stride was taken in a bid to curb corruption, keeping checks and balances to make councilors justify their wealth when alleged or accused of being corrupt. After the intervention by BPRA regarding declaration of assets, a policy was formulated that made it mandatory for councilors and managers in council to declare their assets, financial interests and sources of income. This has to a great extent induced a sense of adherence to professional ethics and standards within the BCC, with duty bearers knowing that they are being closely watched by the residents in their execution of duty.
- CSOs and residents successfully persuaded local authorities to set up gender sensitive and youth friendly structures, which inculcated the use of participatory and inclusive approaches to local governance in the programme selected areas and beyond. The signature achievement in this area, in follow up to Diakonias gender mainstreaming capacity building thrust, was the adoption and introduction of the gender responsive budgeting (GRB) template across all 92 local authorities after Gender Links successfully lobbied for the adoption of the template. According to the Gender Links monitoring report of 2022, the overall percentage allocation of gender responsive budgets in LAs stands at 16.3% against a target of 20%. Umguza Rural District Council is one exemplary local authority which institutionalized gender responsiveness in allocation of resources. Seventy percent (70%) of Umguzas budget is gender responsive. Besides budgets, commitment to gender issues was also reflected in setting up a gender desk, and gender libraries as a form of public service to citizens resourced with gender literature to help bring awareness on gender issues.
- Inclusive civic engagement has resulted in LAs processes, practices, and decisions that are more responsive to community priorities, avoiding many unforeseen consequences, and creating relationships that hold LAs accountable. Partner community score cards have indicated a great improvement in LAs response to calls to urgently attend to water pipe and sewage bursts, and garbage collection, which was not the case when the programme began. In Gwanda CYDT reported of improved youth recreational facilities, while COTRAD reported of improved council responsiveness that has led to rehabilitation of roads and bridges. IYWD reported the reduction of maternity ward fees by the Bindura Municipality after they mobilized citizens and successfully lobbied for the reduction of the exorbitant US-dollar denominated charges. IYWD also narrated some success stories with the construction of disability friendly and girl-child friendly toilets in Pfura RDC.
- Despite the slow movement by parliament in legislating the purpose, function and procedures related to the use of the Constituency Development Fund (CDF). Through the CDF Bill, Consortium partners engaged the Speaker of Parliament to ensure accountability and transparency of CDF usage within constituencies. Consequently, most Members of Parliament formed community committees and established WhatsApp groups that include women, men, and youth groups, to engage them and solicit community views and perspectives in the identification of projects to be funded through the CDF. For example, in Bulawayo, CDF was used to drill boreholes in Luveve. In Mpopoma, residents feedback meetings with the Member of Parliament included demands for receipts and detailed explanation of how the funds were used as part of ensuring transparency and accountability.
- The programme also facilitated the creation of district-based WhatsApp Groups for sharing community information on service delivery and social accountability. The district-based WhatsApp groups were established by members of the Accountability Action Groups (AAGs) as the administrators. Each AAG was able to reach the maximum number of invites to the WhatsApp group which was pegged at 100 young people on 50/50 gender basis. This was a milestone achievement as for the first time in the targeted constituencies, youth appreciated the importance of social media. The platforms were used to mobilise youth and to engage local authorities. The WhatsApp platform increased interaction, connectivity, and coordination among rural communities. The sharing of best practices among the partners culminated in the production of a Best Practice Model booklet, which was shared with other CSO partners outside this programme and funding partners. The booklet will also form the basis of future programme interventions by Diakonia and partners.
